gloss: wordplay; word game; play on words

definitions.gloss: wordplay; word game; play on words
definitions.explanation: Creative or humorous use of language for amusement, including puns, riddles, rhymes, and other linguistic games.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}と{言葉遊|ことばあそ}びをして{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.english: I had fun playing word games with the children.

examples.japanese: しりとりは{日本|にほん}の{代表的|だいひょうてき}な{言葉遊|ことばあそ}びだ。
examples.english: Shiritori is a representative Japanese word game.

examples.japanese: {落語|らくご}には{巧|たく}みな{言葉遊|ことばあそ}びがたくさん{含|ふく}まれていて、{聞|き}き{取|と}るのが{難|むずか}しいこともある。
examples.english: Rakugo contains a lot of clever wordplay, which can sometimes be difficult to catch.

notes:
A compound of {言葉|ことば} (words) + {遊|あそ}び (play). Covers a wide range of linguistic play, from children's games like しりとり (word chain) and なぞなぞ (riddles) to sophisticated literary puns and {掛|か}け{言葉|ことば} (double-meaning words) in poetry and comedy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {言葉遊|ことばあそ}びをする — do wordplay, play word games
- {言葉遊|ことばあそ}びが{好|す}き — like wordplay
- {巧|たく}みな{言葉遊|ことばあそ}び — clever wordplay
- {言葉遊|ことばあそ}びの{本|ほん} — word game book

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {駄洒落|だじゃれ} — pun, bad joke; a specific type of wordplay, often groan-inducing
- {掛|か}け{言葉|ことば} — double entendre, pivot word; a classical rhetorical technique using words with double meanings
- {地口|じぐち} — a type of pun based on similar-sounding phrases; more literary and traditional
